text:
Sam: Heads up — noticed intermittent perf/regression on nightly paged-attn fp8 runs. Softmax outputs showing lots of near-zero values then rare huge spikes; some generations repeat tokens. Profiling attached.
Maya: Can you paste a sample log or minimal repro? :thinking_face:
Sam: log snippet:
```
perf: batch=64 seq=4096 model=redwood-v1-fp8
attention_softmax max=1.2e-3 min=1.2e-45 median=1.3e-5
observed_zeros: 432 / 2048
spike: softmax>1e2 at layer 12 step 13456
```
Jun: That smells like underflow to zero followed by one position dominating after exp -> effectively overflow. If the fp8 path omits a log-sum-exp stabilization or eps clamp we get that.
Olga: Which attention kernel got picked by the selector for that run? fused flash or paged fallback?
Sam: Kernel selector chose fused_flash_fp8_v2 (heuristic: seq>2048 + batch>32). If I force bf16 flash it looks stable.
perf-bot: Benchmark summary: nightly long-seq suite shows avg latency +12% and 0.6% correctness regressions on fp8 fused variant. Regression introduced in commit abc1234 (kernel refactor).
Maya: Can you share the exact repro command? I'll try to run on my rig.
Sam: repro: `python tools/paged_run.py --model redwood-v1 --precision fp8 --seq 4096 --batch 64 --seed 42`
Jun: Also dump qscale / accumulator stats. fp8 quant params can amplify tiny differences. If the softmax denominator gets truncated we end up with subnormal zeros.
Sam: qscale dump shows a few layers with scale ~1.6e-7 before quantization.
Jun: There we go. In fp32/bf16 paths we do `max(x) - max(x)` trick then `exp(x - max)`; in fp8 we optimized away an extra fp32 path and lost the guard. Kernel change probably removed the clamp/eps.
Olga: I remember a GPU tweak to reduce fp32 casts in fused kernels; it avoided extra conversions but may have skipped `+ eps` pre-divide. Risky for very long sequences.
Sam: Quick local hotfix: restored stable_logsumexp path for the fused_fp8 kernel. Local runs: correctness fixed, latency regression reduced to +1.5% vs bf16 baseline. Will open PR with microbenchmark numbers.
Zach: We should gate the fused_fp8 kernel for seq>2048 until we have numeric guards and a regression test. Canary rollout + telemetry.
Maya: +1. Also add a small numeric test into evallist that uses extreme score ranges to catch underflow/overflow in CI.
Sam: Opening PR #4321 now, attaching perf traces and an nvprof snippet showing the softmax values. I'll add a toggle in kernel selector to prefer bf16 for now.
ci-bot: Build queued for PR #4321. Status: queued -> running.
Maya: Nice, thanks Sam. Once CI passes let's run the long-seq nightly harness on canary infra and watch the telemetry for softmax spike events.
Sam: Will do. I'll also add a tiny dataset in unit tests with seed 42 to keep this from regressing again. :lock:
Jun: If we add the clamp, include a test for quantized accumulators too — sometimes the issue shows only after KV cache warmup.
Sam: Good call. I'll include KV warmup case in the test plan.
